facts.statement: Lametasaurus is a dinosaur genus known from the Lameta Formation in Jabalpur, India.
facts.quote: Lametasaurus (; ), is a chimeric genus of dinosaur known from the Lameta Formation of Jabalpur, India.

facts.statement: Lametasaurus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace 70 millones de años durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Subcontinente Indio.

facts.statement: Charles Alfred Matley excavated fossils near Jabalpur between October 1917 and 1919.
facts.quote: Between October 1917 and 1919 Charles Alfred Matley excavated fossils near Jabalpur.

facts.statement: Charles Alfred Matley named the type species Lametasaurus indicus in 1923.
facts.quote: In 1923, he named one of these as the type species Lametasaurus indicus.

facts.statement: The type specimen included dermal scutes, a sacrum 61 cm long, a left ilium 96 cm long, a tibia 58 cm long, and teeth.
facts.quote: The type specimen consisted of a number of dermal scutes, a sacrum of at least five sacral vertebrae (61 cm in length), a pair of ilium (left ilium is 96 cm in length with the acetabular portion, including the pubic and ischial processes, being about 37 cm long and 18 cm wide), a tibia (58 cm cm long with the distal breadth being 23.3 cm) and teeth.

facts.statement: Remains collected by Barnum Brown were initially thought to be part of a tail club but were later identified as a large osteoderm.
facts.quote: In 1933 Matley and Friedrich von Huene described some more remains collected by Barnum Brown, thought to have been part of a tail club; later this was shown to be a large osteoderm.

facts.statement: Alick Walker designated the scutes as the lectotype in 1964, excluding teeth and bones from the type material.
facts.quote: In 1964, Alick Walker chose the scutes as the lectotype, thus removing the teeth and the bones from the type material.

facts.statement: The type material is lost and lacks a known inventory number, hindering the testing of hypotheses.
facts.quote: The type material has been lost, lacking a known inventory number, making it difficult to test the several hypotheses.

facts.statement: Lametasaurus is commonly considered a nomen dubium (dubious name) today.
facts.quote: The taxon is today commonly seen as a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Based on its robust tibia, the estimated weight of Lametasaurus is 3600 kg.
facts.quote: The weight estimate of Lametasaurus, on the basis of the robust tibia, is 3600 kg, similar morphology can be seen in the tibia of Pycnonemosaurus, which indicates similar weight estimates.

facts.statement: Matthew Carrano and colleagues suggested in 2008 that the scutes were likely titanosaurian rather than ankylosaurian.
facts.quote: In 2008, Matthew Carrano e.a. discarded the possibility the scutes were ankylosaurian, stating they were probably titanosaurian, but noted that a comparison to the osteoderms of Ceratosaurus would help in determining its affinities.

facts.statement: The fossil was originally suggested to be a paleontological chimera composed of material from many different animals.
facts.quote: Originalmente se indicó que sería una posible quimera paleontológica compuesta de muchos animales distintos.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the Maastrichtian-aged Lameta Formation, while the species name refers to India.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se refiere a la Formación Lameta, la cual data de la época del Maastrichtiense, mientras que el nombre de la especie es en referencia a la India.

facts.statement: In 2008, Matthew Carrano et al. suggested the scutes might belong to a titanosaur or perhaps an abelisaurid.
facts.quote: En 2008 Matthew Carrano et al. descartaron la posibilidad de que los escudos fueran de un anquilosaurio, estableciendo que podrían ser probablemente de un titanosaurio o quizás de un abelisáurido.

facts.statement: If the scutes belong to an abelisaurid, the species would not be a chimera and could be a senior synonym of Indosaurus or Rajasaurus.
facts.quote: De ser correcto este último caso, la especie no habría sido en principio una quimera y sería un posible sinónimo más antiguo de Indosaurus y/o Rajasaurus.

facts.statement: The loss of the holotype material due to a missing catalog number makes it difficult to evaluate different hypotheses.
facts.quote: El material del holotipo se ha perdido, al carecer de un número conocido de catálogo, lo que hace difícil evaluar las diferentes hipótesis.

facts.statement: The parent group of Lametasaurus is Abelisauridae.
Lametasaurus lived from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.quote: In 1935, Dhirendra Kishore Chakravarti contested the interpretation as an armoured dinosaur. He claimed that the specimen was a chimera including titanosaurid armor, crocodile teeth and theropod hindlimb material.
